choices.text: It keeps moving at a constant 8 m/s

questions.feedback: That stopped answer is the one to unlearn: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped. Reteach point: A flat v-t line means constant velocity: the object keeps moving at the same speed.
questions.misconception: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped.
questions.prompt: A velocity-time graph runs flat at 8 m/s. What is the object doing?

questions.feedback: Scene s2 fixes this: the gradient of a distance-time graph is the speed, and 90 / 30 = 3 metres per second.
questions.prompt: A distance-time graph climbs 90 metres in 30 seconds in a straight line. What is the speed?

questions.feedback: Scene s3: the shaded area growing under the line is the distance travelled - 100 metres in the scene.
questions.prompt: The area under a velocity-time graph gives which quantity?

questions.answer: Displacement is zero because the runner ends where they started, while the distance covered is 800 metres.
questions.feedback: Scene s4: velocity uses displacement, not distance - the outward and return legs cancel, so velocity is zero even though speed is 8 m/s.
questions.prompt: A runner goes 400 metres down a track and back in 100 seconds. Why is the average velocity zero while the average speed is 8 m/s?
